nuances.title: Over-translating domain nouns into shuddh Hindi
nuances.ai_likely_does: Renders core service terms in pure/Sanskritized Hindi — उड़ान (flight), आरक्षण (booking), निरस्तीकरण (cancellation), धनवापसी (refund) — sounding like a news broadcast, not a phone customer.
nuances.native_does: Keeps these in English inside a Hindi matrix: 'मेरी flight cancel हो गई', 'booking change करनी है', 'refund कब आएगा'. Real callers say flight/booking/cancel/refund/seat/PNR in English and inflect Hindi around them.

nuances.title: Wrong gender on verbs/adjectives for a female persona
nuances.ai_likely_does: Defaults to masculine 1st-person forms regardless of persona gender: 'मैं करना चाहता हूँ', 'मैं परेशान हूँ', 'मैंने किया था'.
nuances.native_does: A female speaker uses feminine forms: चाहती हूँ (not चाहता), 'मैंने की थी', 'मैं गई थी'. Agreement must hold across the call, including with objects ('मैंने टिकट बुक की थी').

nuances.title: Honorific-plural verb agreement with आप
nuances.ai_likely_does: Pairs आप with singular verb endings ('आप बता', 'आप कर सकता है') or mixes आप and तुम; uses तुम/तू toward an agent.
nuances.native_does: आप always takes plural agreement and -इए imperative: 'आप बता सकते हैं', 'ज़रा देख लीजिए', 'आप बताइए'. Customer↔agent stays mutually आप; तुम/तू would be rude.

nuances.title: Verbalizing email symbols @ . _ -
nuances.ai_likely_does: Speaks symbols in literal Hindi calques (डॉट as बिंदु, underscore as अधोरेखा, hyphen as योजक) or omits them.
nuances.native_does: Uses the conventional spoken-English tokens embedded in Hindi: 'एट द रेट' (or 'एट') for @, 'डॉट' for ., 'अंडरस्कोर' for _, 'डैश/हाइफ़न' for -, and 'gmail डॉट com'. Local-part letters spelled in English alphabet names.

nuances.title: Phone/PNR digit grouping and 'double'
nuances.ai_likely_does: Reads long numbers as one big Hindi cardinal ('छियानवे करोड़...') or strictly digit-by-digit in Hindi without natural pairing and English 'double'.
nuances.native_does: Reads phone numbers in 2–3 digit chunks, often code-switching to English digits, and uses 'double' for repeats: 'double nine', 'नौ-आठ-सात... double-two'.

nuances.title: Spelling alphanumeric codes (PNR) letter by letter
nuances.ai_likely_does: Pronounces a PNR/booking code as a word or uses Hindi letter names (क ख ग), with no spelling-alphabet anchoring.
nuances.native_does: Spells codes using English letter names with Hindi connectors: 'capital A, फिर 7, Z, K'; agents confirm 'Z for zebra?'-style anchors in English. Codes use the Roman alphabet, not Devanagari.

nuances.title: Missing natural Hindi fillers/hedges
nuances.ai_likely_does: Uses no fillers or only English 'um/uh'; produces clean, written-style sentences.
nuances.native_does: Sprinkles 'मतलब', 'वो क्या है ना', 'actually', 'बस', 'थोड़ा', 'ऐसा है कि', 'यानी'. Hedged openings like 'वो क्या है ना, मेरी flight...' are very common.

nuances.title: Backchannels जी / हाँ जी / अच्छा
nuances.ai_likely_does: Acknowledges with bare 'हाँ' or English 'okay/yes', missing the ubiquitous जी-based backchannels.
nuances.native_does: Uses 'जी', 'जी हाँ', 'हाँ जी', 'अच्छा अच्छा', 'ठीक है जी', 'जी बिल्कुल' as continuers. 'जी?' alone signals 'sorry, come again?'.

nuances.title: Request framing — ज़रा/please and indirect requests
nuances.ai_likely_does: Issues direct imperatives translated from English ('मेरी booking cancel करो') without softeners, or overuses a literal 'कृपया'.
nuances.native_does: Softens with 'ज़रा', 'please' (English), and modal 'क्या आप ... सकते हैं?': 'ज़रा check कर दीजिए ना'. कृपया is written-register; spoken callers prefer ज़रा + please.

nuances.title: Account/telecom/retail terms kept in English
nuances.ai_likely_does: Translates account→खाता, password→कूटशब्द, recharge→पुनःभरण, order→आदेश, network→संजाल.
nuances.native_does: Says account, password/OTP, recharge, plan, order, delivery, network, balance, data in English: 'मेरा OTP नहीं आया', 'recharge fail हो गया', 'order deliver नहीं हुआ'.

nuances.title: Translationese for 'I want to / I would like to'
nuances.ai_likely_does: Calques English politeness: 'मैं चाहूँगा कि...', or stiff 'मुझे ... करने की इच्छा है'.
nuances.native_does: Uses 'मुझे ... करना है' / '... करवाना है': 'मुझे flight cancel करवानी है'. The causative करवाना (get it done by someone) is the natural service-call verb, not plain करना.

nuances.title: Dates and money in native form
nuances.ai_likely_does: Says dates in English order/month names with ordinals ('April fifteenth') or full Hindi cardinals for rupees with paise.
nuances.native_does: Day before month, cardinal day: 'पंद्रह अप्रैल' / '15 तारीख़'; money in rupees with लाख/हज़ार: 'साढ़े तीन हज़ार', 'पाँच हज़ार रुपये'. Uses तारीख़ for 'date' and the lakh system.

nuances.title: 'Has happened / got done' aspect with हो गया
nuances.ai_likely_does: Uses plain present/past calqued from English ('मेरा payment fail है', 'booking cancel है') instead of the resultative.
nuances.native_does: Marks completed events with हो गया/गई: 'payment fail हो गया', 'booking cancel हो गई', 'पैसे कट गए'. 'कट गए' (money got deducted) is the idiomatic complaint phrasing.

nuances.title: Over-formal Sanskritized connectives
nuances.native_does: Spoken register uses 'तो', 'लेकिन/पर', 'क्योंकि', 'और', and ends with 'thank you'/'शुक्रिया' rather than formal धन्यवाद; परंतु/तथा/अतः sound like a textbook.

nuances.title: Opening and closing routines
nuances.ai_likely_does: Opens with a literal 'नमस्ते, मैं आपकी कैसे मदद कर सकता हूँ' from the customer side, or closes with bare English 'bye'.
nuances.native_does: Caller opens 'हाँ जी, हेलो' / 'जी, बात हो रही है ...?' and states the issue; closes 'ठीक है जी, थैंक्यू'. 'हेलो' (not नमस्ते) is the default phone opener.

nuances.title: 'Problem/issue' and complaint vocabulary
nuances.ai_likely_does: Uses समस्या/कठिनाई for every problem and शिकायत-दर्ज stiffly.
nuances.native_does: Says 'problem'/'issue'/'दिक्कत'/'परेशानी': 'मुझे एक दिक्कत आ रही है', 'issue ये है कि...', 'complaint करनी है'. समस्या is fine but दिक्कत/issue dominate calls.

nuances.title: Time of day and relative time
nuances.ai_likely_does: Uses 24-hour or stiff 'पूर्वाह्न/अपराह्न'; literal 'morning ten o'clock'.
nuances.native_does: 12-hour with सुबह/शाम/रात/दोपहर and बजे: 'सुबह दस बजे', 'शाम साढ़े छह बजे'; relative time 'परसों', 'अगले हफ़्ते', 'कल'.
